EQT AB said its third-quarter results were driven by strong asset growth, heavy fundraising momentum and rising value across key holdings, with fee-paying assets under management up €42 billion in the period. The company also raised its fundraising target for the current cycle to €140 billion from €100 billion, helped by the Coller Capital acquisition and strong demand for new strategies. EQT shares rose 3.62% to $291.8 from $281.6, leaving the stock well below its 52-week high of $383 but above the low of $259.

EQT said Q3 was marked by broad-based growth across its platform. The firm reported double-digit value creation in private equity and infrastructure over the past 12 months, while funds in value-creation mode rose 5% in the quarter and 10% over the year.

The company also highlighted a sharp increase in investment income. In the first half of 2026, investment income exceeded €200 million, far above the roughly €10 million recorded for all of 2025 in fee-related performance revenues. EQT said about €20 billion of funds were eligible for fee-related performance revenues at quarter-end.

The quarter also reflected the effect of the Coller Capital deal, which closed at the end of August. EQT said the acquisition strengthened its secondaries business and helped lift the firm to the position of third-largest private markets manager globally. Management said the deal also expanded its reach in insurance capital, one of the fastest-growing funding pools in private markets.

EQT shares gained 3.62% on the latest session, closing at $291.8 versus $281.6 previously. The move suggests investors welcomed the company’s stronger AUM growth, higher fundraising outlook and expanding product mix.

The stock remains below the top end of its 52-week range, which may indicate that some investors are still waiting for more evidence of sustained carry and exit momentum. Even so, the latest move placed the shares comfortably above the yearly low, reflecting a positive response to the quarter’s operating trends.

EQT raised its fundraising-cycle target to €140 billion from the earlier €100 billion goal. Management said the new target reflects the addition of Coller Capital and stronger-than-expected demand for new products.

The company said the Scaleup Europe Fund has already attracted commitments above €3 billion and is likely to end up materially larger than its €5 billion target. The AI Infrastructure Fund is expected to keep growing, with management saying the fee rate should gradually move toward the top end of its 50 to 75 basis point range.

EQT also said it expects continued momentum in its evergreen products, with gross inflows of about €2.5 billion expected in the second half of 2026. The Stockbridge acquisition, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, is projected to add $17 billion to $19 billion in fee-paying AUM and $35 million to $45 million in fee-related EBITDA in 2027.

Per Törnqvist, EQT’s chief executive, said: “After the acquisition of Coller Capital, EQT is now the third largest private markets firm globally.”

He added: “We are the global provider of international alpha. Thanks to the breadth of our platform, we can deliver unique opportunities and differentiated solutions.”

On the AI Infrastructure Fund, Törnqvist said: “All of the value creation that we saw in the quarter relates to earnings growth and new business growth. We haven’t made any changes in the multiple for EdgeConneX.”

Gustav Stenbeck, the company’s chief financial officer, said the real estate business would benefit from the Stockbridge deal over time, but that margins would not reach firm-wide levels in the short to medium term.

Analysts focused on three main topics: the pace of fundraising, the timing of exits and the impact of new acquisitions on margins.

Questions on EQT XI centered on when the fund would be activated and how long fundraising might last. Management said activation depends on the first investment and that fundraising should continue for 12 to 18 months after the first close.

Analysts also pressed on exits, especially the timing of carry recognition from EQT IX and Infra IV. Management said exits do not happen in a straight line and that the company is preparing portfolio companies for both strategic sales and IPOs.

Another major topic was the Stockbridge acquisition. Analysts asked how the deal would affect fee-related EBITDA margins and whether the company still expects long-term margin targets to hold. EQT said the transaction fits its strategy and should support growth, even if it creates some short-term margin pressure.

Questions on the AI Infrastructure Fund also focused on valuation. Management said the quarter’s $1.1 billion increase in EdgeConneX value came entirely from earnings growth and new business, not from a higher valuation multiple.

It also helps us position EQT as the natural partner for global asset allocators that want to get access to private market opportunities in Europe. In our private equity strategies, we can give investors exposure to the demographic and economic growth in Asia. 60% of the economic growth in the world is coming from Asia, but only 5% of the capital raised for private markets funds are invested there. Thanks to joining forces with Coller, we can engage with clients on their strategic asset allocation considerations, we can provide clients with the most attractive liquidity solutions, and we can help them stay invested in their winners and support them in rebalancing their portfolios.

Today, with the acquisition of Stockbridge, we are taking another step in the development of EQT and in making EQT an even more attractive partner for clients. As we stated in our first half update, broadening the thematic focus areas and growing our real estate platform is a strategic priority for us. Performance in EQT Real Estate remains strong, and we want to be able to offer investors access to more alpha in this asset class. We will come back to Stockbridge shortly. Today, we are really in a stronger position than ever before. I have never been more excited about what we are building. In a tricky environment for our industry, we continue to produce attractive deal flow and good returns for investors.

Thanks to our strong local presence in our target geographies, we can unlock attractive investment opportunities in our prioritized sectors. We find those opportunities both in the public markets and in the private markets. We deliver the most compelling co-invest program globally. Over the last 12 months, we doubled our fund-based investments to EUR 30 billion. At the same time, we sent back EUR 29 billion to clients. We will keep on investing in our value creation toolbox, in our AI capabilities, and our capital markets expertise so that we can maintain the attractive value creation momentum in our portfolio and that we can maintain those top quartile DPIs in our key funds. On the back of our strong track record and the strong performance we’ve generated, our fundraising momentum is excellent and we are taking market share.

The secondaries market is one of the fastest-growing areas of the private markets industry. Deal volume in the first half of 2026 is up 20% year-on-year. There are a number of forces behind this structural growth trend, including increasing client demand for liquidity solutions and private market investors wanting to stay invested with their best assets for longer. Our colleagues from Coller EQT give us access to these capabilities and to arguably one of the longest and most consistent track records in the secondaries industry. Across the most recent flagship funds, Coller has delivered first quartile net returns.

In the short term, at Coller EQT, we’re focused on the launch of the fundraisings for the new generation of the private equity and credit secondary funds on capturing the attractive growth opportunity that we’re seeing in the insurance segment, where we really see strong demand for the structuring solutions that Coller EQT can offer. We’re focused on accelerating the product build-out both for our institutional clients and for our wealth clients. We remain confident in the target that we’ve communicated to double Coller’s fee-based assets under management in less than four years. Next slide, please. The latest product addition to the EQT platform is the Scaleup Europe Fund. In this strategy, we’re off to an amazing start. Deal flow is above even our most optimistic assumptions, and it’s clear that Europe doesn’t have a startup problem, but it has a scale-up challenge.

This strategy is perfectly designed to address this challenge and to capture this opportunity. The fund has already announced seven investments, including ICEYE, Europe’s leader in radar satellite intelligence, Tandem Health, a leading European clinical AI platform, and Mistral, the leading European sovereignty AI platform. The pipeline that we see going forward remains deep across geographies, the targeted sub-sectors. I expect the investment pace to remain healthy. Demand from investors globally for this fund is very encouraging. We expect demand to significantly surpass the EUR 5 billion target fund size. Next slide, please. Post being awarded the mandate to manage the Scaleup Europe Fund, EQT has become the preferred partner for talented founders and entrepreneurs. Most of them now want to have EQT and the Scaleup Europe Fund as a shareholder. This is really also what we’re seeing in the attractive deal flow that I just spoke about.

In addition to this, there’s also a broader positive halo effect across all of EQT and the entire EQT platform. The win of this mandate to manage the Scaleup Europe Fund and the way we’re delivering on this strategy has really elevated EQT’s standing globally. Thanks to our track record, EQT being a true European success story, and post the endorsement from the European Commission, EQT is now seen as the partner of choice for founders and global private market investors. Entrepreneurs in Europe are looking for a partner that can give them access to relevant sector expertise, operating capabilities, and really the support to help them win globally. Investors from around the world are turning to EQT for access to the most attractive European investment opportunities and access to the most attractive alpha in Europe.
